premises.text: At crowded venues people fail to find who nearby matters for deals, stories, cofounders, or social goals
premises.evidence_span: stand by the conference bar eating peanuts, wondering who you should talk to next

premises.text: A mobile app finds people at nearby venues, aggregates public profile data, and ranks who is most relevant to you
premises.evidence_span: Sonar scours the web for people at this venue, then aggregates and synthesizes publicly available profile data, and then sorts the room by who's most relevant to you

premises.text: One click shows shared interests, mutual friends, and a bio so strangers become actionable connections
premises.evidence_span: Sonar gives me an instant overview of Fergus and how we're connected

premises.text: Users can send a hyper-targeted introduction with enough social proof to start a conversation in place
premises.evidence_span: you're never more than one click away from a hyper-targeted introduction to the person you want to meet

premises.text: The app enables digital local self-expression—telling people present who you are and what you want
premises.evidence_span: giving you a way to tell people here that you're here and this is what you're about

value.text: Uncover hidden in-person connections so meeting the right person is not left to chance
value.evidence_span: uncovers the hidden connections that you share with everyone else in this room

secondary_value.text: Democratize meatspace / hyperlocal social CRM that saves time and money

causal_links.evidence_span: Are you guys really going to leave that up to chance
bottled the thousands of connections that I definitely would have missed
digital local self-expression that you can use to share what you're proud of and what you're looking for

notes: Three-click flow (rank, overview, intro) kept as facets of one hyperlocal matching mechanism under enumeration cascade, but overview and intro retained as separately worded steps only where they are distinct UI jobs—actually P2/P3/P4 are one product surface; split because speaker frames three sequential value steps that could fail independently (ranking vs proof vs messaging). Singleton D3: self-expression framed as distinct medium beyond CRM tooling.
